title: Groundwater Elevation from Depth-to-Water

GW_elev.units: m or ft (NAVD88 or local datum)

RP_elev.description: Reference point elevation (surveyed top of casing or mark)

DTW.description: Depth to water measured from reference point

applicability: For artesian (flowing) wells, DTW is negative (water above reference point) and GW_elev > RP_elev. Always record measurement point, date, time, and method.

title: Hydraulic Gradient from Well Pairs
applicability: Requires minimum 3 wells (triangle method) to determine gradient magnitude and direction. Two wells give gradient along the line between them only. Wells must be screened in the same aquifer zone.

title: Casing Volume (for Development)

V_casing.description: Volume of water standing in casing

L_water.description: Length of water column in casing (total depth - depth to water)

applicability: Development requires removal of 3–5 casing volumes minimum. 50 mm (2 in) well: ~1.6 L/m (0.16 gal/ft). 100 mm (4 in) well: ~6.5 L/m (0.65 gal/ft). Also include filter pack annular volume for thorough development.

title: Filter Pack Grain Size Selection

D50_filter.description: Median grain size of filter pack sand

D50_formation.description: Median grain size of aquifer formation

applicability: For uniform formations (Cu < 3). For well-graded formations (Cu > 6): D50_filter = 6–9 × D30_formation. Screen slot size ≈ D10 of filter pack (retains 90% of pack). If formation is unknown, use commercial filter sand (1–2 mm).
source: Driscoll (1986) Groundwater and Wells, ASTM D5092

title: Barometric Efficiency
applicability: Confined aquifers: BE = 0.2–0.8 (water level responds inversely to barometric changes). Unconfined: BE ≈ 0 (atmospheric pressure transmitted directly to water table). Must correct non-vented transducer data for barometric effects.

title: Three-Point Method — Gradient Direction
equation: Gradient direction determined by: (1) interpolate head at point on line between highest and lowest wells equal to intermediate well head, (2) gradient is perpendicular to this line, pointing from high to low
applicability: Minimum 3 non-collinear wells in same aquifer. For more than 3 wells, use contouring (kriging) or plane-fitting. Gradient direction = flow direction in isotropic aquifer. In anisotropic aquifer, flow direction deviates from gradient direction.

title: Annular Grout Volume
applicability: Grout must be tremied from bottom-up to prevent bridging. Cement-bentonite grout: 1 bag (94 lb) Portland cement + 3–5% bentonite by weight of water + 6–7 gal water ≈ 1.2 ft³ of grout.
source: ASTM D5092, state well construction standards
